about.checks.1: Assure reads every document and keeps each figure tied to its source page. A language model then writes the draft. A formal consistency checker then tests whether the draft's figures and the values locked from the source can all be true at the same time. For a labeled figure, the language model does not make that call. For a sentence with no label, the language model turns it into a numeric comparison, and the formal consistency checker tests whether it holds. When a file is first read, the formal consistency checker can also flag figures in that file that contradict each other.
about.checks.2: Red-Hat review is separate, and it runs only when someone asks for it. A language model reads the draft the way a skeptical reviewer would and tries to find what is wrong: a mismatch with the attached source sentence, an overstatement, a missing clause, or a figure that needs a citation. It does not decide the numeric conflict. The review screen shows the contradiction and export is flagged. A person accepts or rejects each finding. The file can still be downloaded.

terms.accuracy: AI systems are probabilistic and can hallucinate. Verification is a filter, not a promise of accuracy. We do not promise that output is flawless, complete, or free from errors. Independently verify critical information.
terms.advice: Assure performs document analysis, verification, and compilation. It does not give legal, financial, or professional advice. Consult qualified professionals before you act on any output.
terms.answers: Assure rewrites your question, can send it to models you connect, and can drop claims that were not in your files. That is a filter, not a promise of accuracy. You check the result before you use it with a client, a paper, or a decision.
terms.as_is: The software is provided "as is", without warranties. We are not liable for damages or other consequences of your use. We do not promise uptime, accuracy, or fitness for a particular job. Any service levels are set only in your signed enterprise agreement.

solutions.cards.1.name: Invoice vs contract
solutions.cards.1.finding: The invoice total is 142,500 EUR. The contract cap is 120,000 EUR. The difference is 22,500 EUR above the cap. Both source pages stay open, and the mismatch is flagged before payment.
solutions.cards.2.name: Claims
solutions.cards.2.finding: A claim file is checked against the policy and the supporting invoices. The billed amount is compared with the policy terms, the certificate on file is compared with the claim, and every figure keeps its source page.
solutions.cards.3.name: Compliance pack
solutions.cards.3.finding: Every certificate and form in the pack is checked against its source. The certificate number on the form did not match the certificate, so the mismatch is marked.
solutions.cards.4.name: Internal report
solutions.cards.4.finding: The report is checked against the sales records and locked volumes. The volume on the report is different from the sales records, so the figure is flagged before the report goes out.
about.who.1: Finance: supplier invoices checked against contract caps and agreed terms before the payment run, with the contract page open next to the invoice.
about.who.2: Claims: claim files checked against policies and the supporting documents that back each figure, before the payout.
about.who.3: Procurement: tenders and supplier packs checked against requirements and the documents behind each bid.
about.proof: The side-by-side example is the proof: a 142,500 EUR invoice is checked against a 120,000 EUR contract cap, both source pages stay open, the difference of 22,500 EUR is marked, and the mismatch is flagged before payment.
arch.flow.1.text: Assure reads both documents side by side and keeps the page, cell, or row for every figure it extracts, so the source stays reachable.
arch.flow.2.text: Figures are compared one to one. Where two labeled numbers cannot both be true at the same time, the conflict is marked on the review screen.
arch.flow.3.text: The document cannot be exported while a contradiction is unresolved. Export blocked on the review screen. A person or an agent decides, and the file can still be downloaded.
arch.flow.4.text: A person or an agent decides, and the file can still be downloaded.
